text:
morgan: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking out loud about reverse-delta rollback for air-gapped upgrades. Idea: ship a tiny "reverse-delta" alongside each staged activation so rollback only needs a small apply, not a full reseed.

sana: Interesting. Is reverse-delta different from our existing staged delta bundles?

morgan: Yeah — staged deltas are forward patches. Reverse-delta is a compact undo patch that applies to the activated state and returns it to prior manifest. Size should be << full bundle.

lee: Biggest concern is correctness and atomicity. If undo fails mid-apply we could end up wedged. How do we guarantee idempotence?

morgan: Two parts: 1) make reverse-deltas content-addressed and checksumed; 2) apply via the same two-phase activation we use for forward bundles (download -> validate -> staged-activate -> final-swap). If final-swap fails, we can fall back to previous symlink.

kim: What about operator UX? They need to see the delta chain to decide safe rollback. Would we expose: `current -> reverse-delta-1 -> reverse-delta-2` ?

ben: We should avoid long chains. Maybe only keep N reverse-deltas (configurable), and prefer checkpoint+single reverse-delta from checkpoint to previous stable.

arch-bot: Note: existing seed agents expect monotonic forward sequence numbers. Reverse-deltas introduce negative sequence ops. Need API change.

ops-bot: Deployment note: airgapped customers often have limited disk. Keeping many reverse deltas might fail. Consider streaming reverse-deltas off operator workstation during rollback instead of storing.

morgan: Good call. Option A: persist 1 reverse-delta per activation on-device. Option B: store XOR-compressed reverse-deltas in external seed cache (operator-managed USB). Option C: stream-only (no local persistence).

sana: Tradeoffs: A = simplest UX, B = middle ground, C = lowest on-device disk but highest runtime complexity. We should pick defaults.

lee: Security: reverse deltas must be signed with the same signing chain as forward bundles, otherwise attacker can craft bogus rollbacks. Also audit logs must record rollbacks as special high-severity events.

kim: Edge-case: what if a forward bundle included schema migrations that are irreversible? Reverse-delta cannot fully undo DB migrations. We need preflight checks and a hard guard: no reverse-delta created for irreversible ops.

ben: Implementation sketch:
```
manifest: {
  prev_manifest: sha256:xxxx,
  activation_ts: 2024-11-12T14:00:00Z,
  reverse_delta_sha: sha256:yyyy
}
```
Reverse-delta payload = list of file ops + metadata + signature. Apply path uses same operator confirmations as forward rollout.

morgan: Also propose a "rollback-policy" flag per release: allowed/forbidden/manual-only. Default: manual-only for any release with irreversible migrations.

arch-bot: RFC note: this impacts verifier agent API and activation state machine. We'll need a short followup RFC to add reverse-delta lifecycle and retention config.

ops-bot: One more ops concern: telemetry. Emit rollback start/finish, bytes transferred, and revert-success boolean to the console (or operator log) so support can correlate.

morgan: Next steps: I'll draft a focused follow-up RFC covering: artifact format, signing, agent API changes, retention defaults, and operator UX. Any objections to prioritizing this for next sprint?

sana: +1 from me.

lee: +1, but add explicit test plan for interrupted revert.

kim: +1. include migration detection heuristics.

ben: +1. add storage budget guidance for airgapped customers. :thumbsup:
